question: What kind of drug is misoprostol?
explanation: Misoprostol is made to copy prostaglandin E1, which naturally helps the cervix soften and triggers uterine contractions. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h1)

question: Why is using misoprostol by itself very common in areas with limited healthcare resources?

options.A: It is widely available, affordable, and effective on its own
options.B: It completely prevents all normal cramping and heavy bleeding
options.C: It removes the need for any follow-up care
options.D: It works twice as fast as other drug combos

explanation: Because mifepristone is hard to get in many places, using misoprostol alone provides a practical and accessible option for safe care. Great job! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h1)

question: What are the two main ways misoprostol affects the uterus and cervix?

options.A: Decreasing blood flow and acting as local anesthesia
options.B: Stimulating contractions and causing cervical ripening
options.C: Blocking progesterone and shrinking the placenta
options.D: Paralyzing the muscle and closing the cervix tightly

explanation: Think of it as doing a two-step job: it softens the cervix so tissue can pass, and it helps the uterine muscle contract to push things out. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h2)

question: How do uterine contractions help during a medical abortion?

options.A: They push the gestational sac down and out through the dilated cervix
options.B: They raise blood pressure to flush out toxins
options.C: They permanently numb pelvic nerves so there is zero pain
options.D: They seal off the uterine lining to stop hormones

explanation: Once the cervix is soft, those rhythmic uterine contractions create the gentle pressure needed to clear the pregnancy tissue safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h2)

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

options.C: A history of high blood pressure

explanation: Misoprostol cannot treat a pregnancy outside the uterus. Giving it would dangerously delay emergency surgery. Always check for this first! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h3)

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h3)

question: Which way of taking misoprostol gets into the bloodstream the fastest?
explanation: Placing the pills under the tongue (sublingual) lets them absorb super fast into the blood vessels right there in the mouth. Brilliant shortcut! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h4)

question: What is a great benefit of using the vaginal route for misoprostol?

options.A: It works instantly in under five minutes
options.B: It means you don't need to know how far along the pregnancy is
options.C: It completely stops all cramping pain
options.D: It results in fewer gastrointestinal side effects like nausea

explanation: Vaginal use skips the stomach processing, which helps many patients avoid nasty stomach upset and vomiting. Smart clinical choice! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h4)

question: Why is an ultrasound or accurate dating so important before giving misoprostol?

options.A: To measure the pelvic muscles for pushing
options.B: To check the patient's exact blood type
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bill
options.D: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy and verify gestational age

explanation: We always double-check that the pregnancy is inside the uterus and within safe limits before starting. Patient safety comes first! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h5)

question: What important advice should a nurse give a patient using the misoprostol-only method?

options.A: It has a 100 percent success rate on the first try
options.B: It requires staying in the hospital for three days
options.C: It has a higher rate of incomplete abortion than combination regimens
options.D: It never causes any physical discomfort

explanation: Being honest helps patients know that a follow-up visit might be needed since misoprostol alone isn't quite as strong as combination drugs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h5)

question: What causes a mild fever and chills shortly after taking misoprostol?

options.A: A sudden drop in body temperature from blood loss
options.B: An allergic reaction to the pill ingredients
options.D: The normal systemic pharmacologic action of prostaglandins

explanation: Prostaglandins can tweak the body's thermostat briefly, causing temporary chills and low fever that go away on their own. Nothing to panic about! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h6)

question: A patient calls 4 hours after taking misoprostol saying they have strong cramps, heavy bleeding with small clots, and mild nausea. What do you tell them?

options.A: Tell them to take a double dose of pills
options.B: Send them straight to the ER for a blood transfusion
options.C: Schedule emergency surgery for a hemorrhage
options.D: Tell the patient these are expected signs that the medication is working

explanation: Cramping and bleeding mean the drug is doing its job! Reassuring the patient builds trust and reduces panic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h6)

question: Which symptom means a patient might be bleeding too much and needs urgent help?

options.A: Spotting light pink discharge for two weeks
options.B: Passing just one blood clot the size of a coin
options.C: Soaking two heavy pads per hour for two consecutive hours
options.D: Having mild cramping that gets better with rest

explanation: Soaking two big pads every hour for two hours straight is our red-flag sign for heavy bleeding that needs immediate medical review. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h7)

question: Which sign strongly points to a uterine infection instead of normal side effects?

options.A: Nausea that goes away in a day
options.B: Chills lasting only for the first two hours
options.C: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and persistent fever
options.D: Cramping that feels worse than a normal period

explanation: Bad-smelling discharge and a fever that sticks around past day one are classic warning signs of infection like endometritis. Good to spot early! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h7)

question: When can a patient get pregnant again after a misoprostol medical abortion?

options.A: After six months for the uterus to heal
options.B: Never, because medical abortion causes permanent sterility
options.C: Immediately, as ovulation can resume before the next period
options.D: Only after waiting three normal menstrual cycles

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! Ovulation can happen even before the very first post-abortion period arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h8)

question: Why is it important to talk about birth control before the patient leaves the clinic?

options.A: To make sure the hospital gets paid by insurance
options.B: To prevent unwanted repeat pregnancies given the rapid return of ovulation
options.C: To push the patient into long-term hormone use
options.D: To make sure the abortion pills keep working

explanation: Since fertility returns so quickly, offering birth control right away protects our patients from unplanned repeat pregnancies. Excellent nursing care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h8)
